Subject: VPC boarding & access orientation — initial checklist

Hi Sahil,

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier — excited to get Acrux onto a Private deployment (VPC) with us. To keep the intake quick and reduce back-and-forth, attached is a short VPC onboarding checklist and a network diagram stub. Can you confirm the items below so we can finalize the private deployment schedule?

- VPC CIDR you'd like us to peer with / accept traffic from (e.g. 10.10.0.0/16)
- Public egress pattern: do you prefer routed NAT (centralized) or per-subnet NAT?
- KMS region / key alias for envelope encryption
- List of IPs that will need access to the management/control plane (we'll provide Redwood egress IPs as well)
- Preferred 2-hour go-live window (timezone aware)

Attachments:
- vpc-onboarding-checklist.docx (checklist + evidence table)
- network-diagram-v2.pdf (starter diagram; we can update after your confirmation)

If it's easier I can propose two 30-min windows for a technical handoff; otherwise reply with the three bullet items above and we'll proceed.

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: VPC boarding & access orientation — port/egress details

Michael / Ben,

Looping in the technical requirements so we can send a concise allowlist to Acrux. Per our runtime and control plane we need the following TCP/UDP ports outbound/inbound (customer-initiated flows):

- Control plane (outbound from Redwood to customer endpoints): TCP 443 to customer endpoints for API callbacks (we'll need CIDR when confirmed).
- Model serving ingress (customer -> Redwood): customers connect to our private endpoint via mTLS over TCP 443. Provide your peering private range and we'll bind the endpoint there.
- KV / cache traffic: TCP 6379 (if using managed Redis) — recommend we keep this within peered/private subnets only.
- Monitoring/metrics push: TCP 8125/UDP 8125 (statsd) only if you opt-in to push metrics; otherwise we'll scrape via a secure exporter over 443.

Firewall snippet for ops team to paste: (example)
- Allow: From 10.40.0.0/24 -> Redwood-private-endpoint (TCP 443)
- Allow: From Redwood-egress-ips -> 10.40.0.0/16 (TCP 443, 6379)

I'll attach the current egress IP list (internal) for the initial handoff — we'll update if we enable burst/alternative regions.

Attachments:
- egress-ip-list.txt

Kimberly Park

kimberly.park@redwood.com

Sahil

Subject: Re: VPC boarding & access orientation — final preflight and next steps

Hi Sahil / team,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the firewall screenshot. A few final items before we declare the environment ready for a staged cutover:

1) Authentication model — if you're not using mTLS initially, we'll rely on source-IP allowlisting + a bearer token for API calls. For longer-term production we strongly recommend mTLS; we can schedule a follow-up to enable that after day-1.

2) Source IP expectations — OK for now to accept 52.200.100.45 as the NATed source for your outbound flows. We'll add a short window on our side to accept that address for the initial tests. Please provide any additional egress IPs if they change.

3) Evidence checklist — outstanding items we need uploaded to the shared Drive: signed KMS policy snippet, procurement SOW, and a completed 'network evidence' tab from vpc-onboarding-checklist.docx. Once those are present we'll lock the go-live window.

4) Proposed cutover: 2026-12-09 02:00–04:00 UTC — we will do a dry-run 24 hours prior (2026-12-08 02:00–03:00 UTC) to exercise end-to-end. Can you confirm both windows?

5) Docs & links: HubSpot record -> https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACRUX-001; Drive folder -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-redwood-onboarding-acrux

Next steps for Redwood:
- I will provision the private endpoint in your peered subnet after we get the final evidence items.
- Ben will own the dry-run on 12/08 and will coordinate runbook steps.

If all good, reply with a single-line confirm for the two windows and any remaining egress IPs.

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
